name: TAROK DANISH
description: Danish Tarok (Grosstarock) is a three-player trick-taking game using a 78-card tarot deck (21 trumps, Fool, 4 suits of 14). Primary objective: win the last trick with the lowest trump (trump 1) or a King. Secondary: win tricks and capture counting cards. Alliances form during play. Each player gets 25 cards (dealer gets 3 extra then discards to 25). Declarations at start: trump holdings, matadors (Fool, lowest trump, 21), court combinations. Two pots (king pot, lowest-trump pot). Card values: 4 for trump 21, lowest trump, Fool, Kings; 3 Queens; 2 Knights; 1 Jacks. Closely related to German Grosstarock; survives mainly in Denmark.

Danish Tarok is the surviving form of German Grosstarock (Grosstarok), introduced in Germany around 1720; now played mainly in Denmark. 78-card tarot, 3 players, lowest-trump/King ultimo and two pots.

Three active players. With four people, the player opposite the dealer sits out and does not play; that player shuffles the spare pack. Play is counter-clockwise; the player to the dealer's right leads to the first trick.
25 cards each; dealer gets 3 extra then discards to 25

items.text: Fool never discard: Some play that the Fool can never be discarded; dealer cannot play for Tout if holding the Fool.
Trump discard reveal: Some play that if the dealer discards trumps, when he shows void of trumps he must if asked declare how many trumps he discarded.
Historic lowest-trump discard: Formerly it was legal to discard the lowest trump (but not Mondo) to create a void in trumps; modern clubs use the rule that Ultimo cards can never be discarded.
